title: Small-team SDK Boot Heuristics and Checklist
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, pragmatic playbook for bootstrapping an SDK integration when the consumer is a small engineering team (1–4 engineers) that needs a working prototype in 3–10 working days. The tone is intentionally informal: checklist-driven guidance, heuristics, and minimal friction patterns that let a tiny team ship a usable sample, CI smoke tests, and clear telemetry.

Scope / Audience:
- Audience: small product or platform teams evaluating or embedding Redwood SDKs
- Languages covered: Node (JS/TS) and Python (short examples) — aim for parity but minimal duplication.
- Output: a runnable sample app, CI smoke job, sample instrumentation, one-pager README.
- Not in scope: internal launcher infra, deep custom auth flows, enterprise-only private-deploy templates.

Constraints & Heuristics (tradeoffs we accept for speed):
- Minimal plumbing: use Redwood hosted API keys for dev samples (do not require VPC).
- Favor clarity over abstraction: explicit example over perfect library design.
- No heavy infra: use GitHub Actions or equivalent for CI smoke test.
- Telemetry: drop-in, low-noise telemetry (basic request counts, latency p50/p95, error rate).

Quickstart outline (3–10 day plan):
Day 0 — Kickoff (1–2 hrs)
- Align owners, pick target feature (text generation, chat, or embeddings), pick language (node or python), and pick sample app type (CLI/demo web).
- Create a repo: github.com/<team>/sdk-quickstart-<lang>
- Create README scaffold with 1-sentence goal, quickstart command, and troubleshooting notes.

Day 1 — First working sample (4–8 hrs)
- Add minimal dependency and wiring:
  - Node: npm init + install @redwoodai/sdk (fake package name for example)
  - Python: pip install redwood-sdk
- Implement a single file example that:
  - Auths with env var REDWOOD_API_KEY
  - Calls the endpoint to generate 1 short response
  - Prints response and logs latency
- Quick manual test locally: node index.js / python main.py

Day 2 — Basic CI + smoke test (2–4 hrs)
- Add GitHub Actions workflow that runs the sample against a recorded API key (use a limited test key or mocked responses).
- CI should verify: exit code 0, response contains expected shape or sample token count, latency < 5s for baseline.

Day 3 — README polish + telemetry + checklist (1–3 hrs)
- README: quickstart section, env vars, runbook, common errors.
- Instrument: emit simple metrics to console and an optional statsd sink.
- Add a small section on cost expectations: sample token counts and estimated cost for a single run.

Optional Days 4–10 — Extras (pick 1–2)
- Add streaming example or function calling snippet.
- Add local mock mode (simple stub server) for offline demos.
- Add a simple UI component (React) and one-click deploy script (Vercel).

Minimal sample scaffolds (copy-paste friendly)
Node (index.js):
const Redwood = require('@redwoodai/sdk');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
(async () => {
  const start = Date.now();
  try {
    const r = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-lite-1', prompt: 'Write a 2-line summary of Redwood Inference' });
    console.log('response:', r.text);
    console.log('latency_ms:', Date.now() - start);
    process.exit(0);
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('call failed', err.message);
    process.exit(2);
  }
})();

Python (main.py):
from redwood import RedwoodClient
import os, time
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
start = time.time()
try:
    r = client.generate(model='redwood-lite-1', prompt='Summarize Redwood Inference in two lines')
    print('response:', r.text)
    print('latency_ms:', int((time.time() - start)*1000))
    raise SystemExit(0)
except Exception as e:
    print('call failed', str(e))
    raise SystemExit(2)

Checklist (working prod-lite checklist)
- [ ] Repo created and README scaffolded (owner: @owner)
- [ ] Single-file sample runs locally with env var REDWOOD_API_KEY (owner: dev)
- [ ] CI workflow runs sample with smoke key or recorded mock (owner: devops)
- [ ] Basic telemetry exists (counts, p50/p95, errors) and logs to console (owner: eng)
- [ ] README contains quickstart, common errors, local mock instructions (owner: docs)
- [ ] Sample includes cost note and token estimate for the example prompt (owner: product)
- [ ] Small test matrix (node/python, local/CI, mock/real) is documented (owner: qa)
- [ ] Security note: ensure no prod key in CI; use secrets manager (owner: sec)

Greedy failure modes and mitigations (fast heuristics)
- Failure: No API key or bad key -> detect and print actionable message, fail fast in CI.
- Failure: Large token responses cause flakiness -> cap max_tokens in samples and include a short prompt.
- Failure: Network flakiness in CI -> use small retry with exponential backoff or run against a recorded fixture.
- Failure: Cost spikes from test runs -> document expected tokens and include guardrails (per-run token cap).

Testing matrix (minimal):
- Node: local interactive run, CI smoke job (mocked or limited-scope key)
- Python: same as node
- Mock mode: stub server in tests to validate request shapes and basic semantics

Telemetry + Observability (low friction)
- Emit: request count, status (ok/error), latency_ms (p50/p95), tokens_out estimate.
- Where: console for sample, optional push to statsd/prometheus if team has it.
- Alerts: set a trivial alert for CI smoke failures; for internal demos, watch for >10% failure rate in nightly runs.

Docs/README outline (one-pager):
- Goal (1 line)
- Quickstart (3 lines)
- Running locally (commands)
- CI smoke test (how to run)
- Troubleshooting (3 most common errors)
- Telemetry (what we collect)
- Security notes (where keys live)
- Next steps (optional extras)

Ownership & handoff
- Minimum handoff doc: 1-page confluence note linking repo, CI, linear/jira ticket, and who to ping in Slack (#devexp).
- Handoff checklist: is README enough for a new engineer to run in <15 minutes? If no, keep iterating until yes.

Common prompts / sample prompts to include in README
- Summarize Redwood Inference in 2 lines.
- Convert this short bullet list into a one-paragraph onboarding blurb.
- Generate 3 test utterances we can use for fuzzing.

Open Questions / TODOs (items to resolve during spike)
- Do we provide a tiny client library wrapper or recommend direct HTTP usage for small teams?
- Mocking strategy: use VCR-style recordings or a tiny stub server?
- Default model choice — pick a model in the catalog that balances cost/latency for samples.
- Should the sample include a streaming example or is that an extra?

Next steps (immediate):
1) Create repo and README scaffold (owner: Evan)
2) Wire basic single-file sample in chosen language (owner: Priya)
3) Add CI smoke job with recorded fixture (owner: Lina)
4) Draft 1-page confluence handoff (owner: Evan)

Notes to self (rough)
- Keep examples intentionally dumb/simple; small teams rarely read complex abstractions.
- Make the README the canonical starting point — it should open with the one-liner used in demos.
- When in doubt, prefer the workflow that reduces the number of manual steps to get a response.

Slack references: #devexp, #platform-infra
JIRA backlog: JIRA-3212 (sample repo + CI), JIRA-3330 (telemetry sketch)
Confluence: DEVEXP-BOOT (boot playbook)
GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-starter (example starter repo)

-- end of playbook --
